strengths: The paper addresses an important practical problem and proposes a potentially useful unified search over pipeline, data, tensor, and fully sharded data parallelism, including memory, topology, and resharding costs.

The evaluation covers diverse hardware—V100, TITAN Xp, A100, and DCU clusters—and several language and vision Transformers. Reported measured gains are meaningful, including 1.41x for ViT-Huge, 1.37x for Swin-Huge, and 3.80x for Llama-7B in selected settings.

The ablations contrasting unified, inter-layer-only, and intra-layer-only search support the value of the enlarged strategy space. The scalability experiment, cost-estimation analysis, and BERT case study provide additional useful evidence.
The manuscript is generally well organized, with explicit notation, an optimization formulation, implementation settings, and readable figures and tables.
weaknesses: Material: The central formulation is not an MIQP as written. Equations (3) and (4) contain terms such as P_ui P_vi (S_u^T R_uv S_v), which are fourth-degree products of decision variables. No auxiliary product variables or linking constraints are given to reduce these terms to quadratic form, so the stated program cannot directly support the claimed Gurobi implementation.

Material: The constraints do not enforce topological ordering of pipeline stages or require graph edges to connect the same or consecutive forward stages. For a simple chain, placing an earlier layer in stage 2 and a later layer in stage 1 can satisfy the per-stage contiguity constraints, while Equation (4) charges only stage j to j+1 communication. Such assignments can therefore omit required communication costs.

Material: Repeated claims of finding an optimal strategy are not justified. Appendix E permits termination at a 4% MIP gap or after 60 seconds; throughput is optimized through an approximate cost model; and the search is restricted to GPipe, equal-sized stage device groups, and pipeline and micro-batch counts that divide n and B. At most, the method approximately optimizes this restricted modeled space.

Material: The specified GPipe memory model appears inconsistent with Algorithm 1. The algorithm passes micro-batch size b=B/c to the cost model, while GPipe without activation checkpointing retains activations from multiple micro-batches. Since c is not supplied to the memory model, Equation (5) can substantially underestimate activation memory if implemented as described.

The cost-model validation reports error only for the strategies selected on EnvA and EnvB. It does not evaluate ranking correlation or selection regret across candidate strategies and excludes the Llama/DCU settings underlying major claims. Thus, an average 3.59% error does not establish that the chosen strategy is the actual throughput optimum.

The comparative evidence is uneven: Alpa is unavailable or fails for several models, the closely related Piper planner is not benchmarked, and the DCU experiment compares against manual enumeration and an unusable DeepSpeed configuration. The scalability study also increases batch size with device count, demonstrating weak rather than fixed-workload scaling.

Reproducibility is limited by the absence of a code link and insufficient specification of the candidate strategy dictionary, profiling procedure, execution-plan transformation, number of independent runs, and meaning of the reported deviations. Reported optimization time excludes profiling overhead and relies on proprietary Gurobi.

The direct contribution to computer vision is limited: the method is primarily a distributed-training systems contribution, with only two vision architectures evaluated and no validation of training convergence or task accuracy.

strengths: The manuscript :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-03/reviews/cvpr2025--gpt56_sol/review-experiment-euqfngo8/call-3a2933467c174111b5aa12bb54c32421/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"} addresses an important practical problem: jointly selecting pipeline placement and per-layer DP/TP/FSDP strategies. A unified discrete-optimization treatment is appealing and potentially useful.

The evaluation covers six model configurations from five Transformer families and four distinct V100, TITAN Xp, A100, and DCU environments. Notable measured results include 1.20–1.71x gains on several ENVB comparisons, 3.80x for Llama-7B on ENVC, and approximately linear throughput scaling from 16 to 64 DCUs.

The restricted-search ablation supports the central intuition that jointly considering inter- and intra-layer choices can outperform either space alone. The BERT case study also makes the resulting hybrid PP/DP/TP/FSDP strategy interpretable.
The paper is generally readable, and the appendix provides useful hardware, model, batch-size, solver, estimation-error, and topology details.
weaknesses: The central formulation is not an MIQP as written. Equations (3) and (4) contain degree-four products such as P_ui P_vi(S_u^T R_uv S_v), while Equation (5) is bilinear; these are nonlinear constraints rather than a quadratic objective with linear constraints. No joint-assignment auxiliary variables or linearization is supplied, and the max term is likewise not reformulated. Consequently, it is unclear how the stated formulation can be submitted to Gurobi 10.1 or reproduced.

The placement constraints do not enforce pipeline-stage order. Equations (6a–c) ensure that each individual stage contains a contiguous subgraph but do not relate different stage indices. For example, a chain edge u→v may assign u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 while satisfying the reported constraints; Equation (4), which charges only transitions j→j+1, then omits that boundary cost. Descending or nonadjacent transitions can therefore be invalid or systematically under-costed.

The GPipe memory and timing models have consequential omissions. CostModeling receives micro-batch size b=B/c, and activation memory is computed from b, but with checkpointing disabled GPipe retains activations for multiple forward micro-batches before backward; the reported memory expression has no dependence on c. Equation (2) also combines forward and backward costs into one bottleneck, which is exact only when their bottleneck stage coincides—an assumption justified merely as occurring with “high probability.” Thus feasibility and modeled iteration time are not technically established.

The repeated claim of finding an optimal strategy is unsupported. The solver has a 60-second limit and can stop at a 4% MIP gap, costs are approximate, and pipeline degrees and micro-batch counts are restricted to divisors. The 3.59% estimation result covers only eight selected solutions and does not measure ranking accuracy or regret over the candidate space; Figure 8 also displays negative values despite defining REE with an absolute value.

The empirical evidence is uneven. The headline 3.80x gain comes from one Llama-7B/A100 comparison, several rows tie the baseline or slightly underperform it, and many competitors are unavailable or fail. The 16–64-device scaling study has no automatic-parallelism baseline, while UniAP merely matches Megatron throughput on the 32-DCU results. Independent run counts are not reported, and the claimed planning-time advantage excludes initial profiling, making the practical 107x comparison difficult to assess.

Reproducibility remains limited: no code is provided, and essential details such as construction of the strategy dictionary, the missing polynomial reformulation, profiling protocol, candidate counts, and baseline tuning are absent; the implementation also depends on proprietary Gurobi. For CVPR specifically, the contribution is primarily generic distributed-training systems work, with only throughput measurements on two vision models and no computer-vision task or accuracy analysis. These substantive correctness and evidence gaps outweigh the promising systems idea in the current manuscript.

No auxiliary variables or exact reduction is reported, so the claimed formulation is technically incomplete and unreproducible.

The placement constraints do not explicitly require every graph edge to remain within one stage or advance from stage j to j+1. Contiguity alone permits reversed or skipped stage indices, while Equation (4) charges only j-to-j+1 edges, potentially omitting communication. The memory model is also ambiguous because Algorithm 1 passes micro-batch size B/c although checkpoint-free GPipe retains activations for multiple micro-batches.

Claims of finding an optimal solution are unsupported: Gurobi is capped at 60 seconds and may stop at a 4% MIP gap, yet solver statuses and final gaps are not reported. Moreover, the cost model is approximate and the search excludes valid configurations such as non-divisible or single-micro-batch pipelines. Treating the capped MIQP solve as constant time also does not constitute a valid complexity analysis of exact optimization.

The experiments establish practical promise but not global optimality or clean causal attribution. The headline 3.80x gain comes from one Llama configuration; Alpa is unavailable for Swin and Llama, several comparisons are OOM/timeout cases, and framework differences confound strategy quality. Cost accuracy is measured only on selected plans rather than across candidates, and Figure 8 displays signed errors despite Equation (13) defining an absolute error.

Reproducibility is limited by the absence of code, software-stack versions, complete strategy-dictionary construction, profiling protocol, and sufficient implementation detail for the cost matrices and execution planner. The contribution is also primarily a general distributed-systems result; its direct computer-vision evidence is limited to throughput on ViT and Swin without a vision-task or numerical-correctness evaluation. These concerns affect the core formulation and claims, so they outweigh the otherwise meaningful systems results.

strengths: The paper targets an important practical problem: jointly selecting pipeline, data, tensor, and fully sharded parallelism instead of optimizing inter- and intra-layer choices hierarchically. The profile-to-cost-model-to-optimizer workflow is potentially useful.

The evaluation spans V100, TITAN Xp, A100, and Hygon DCU environments, up to 64 accelerators, and includes both vision and language Transformers. Actual measured throughput shows meaningful gains in several settings, including 3.80× for Llama-7B and 1.18–1.37× for ViT-Huge/Swin-Huge over available baselines.

The manuscript includes strategy-space ablations, scaling experiments, cost-estimation measurements, and a concrete BERT strategy case study. Hardware, model, batch-size, and Gurobi configurations are reported more thoroughly than is typical.

The exposition is generally readable, with helpful diagrams, notation, pseudocode, and appendices. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-03/reviews/cvpr2025--gpt56_sol/review-experiment-eh4bd5q9/call-6f18b35753b14811b2dce011c9f62f25/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}
weaknesses: The central formulation is not an MIQP as written. Equations (3) and (4) contain products such as P_ui P_vi (S_u^T R_uv S_v), which are degree four in the binary variables, while the maximum in Equation (2) is also not reformulated. No auxiliary-variable linearization is supplied. This is a material gap in the paper's principal technical contribution and prevents reproducing the claimed Gurobi model.

The listed constraints do not enforce monotonic pipeline-stage order. For a chain edge u→v, assigning u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 satisfies the contiguity and placement constraints, yet Equation (4) charges only edges from stage j to j+1 and can assign zero communication cost. Edges crossing nonconsecutive stages are likewise unmodeled. Thus the presented feasible set admits invalid or under-costed plans.

The GPipe memory model appears to undercount activations. UOP passes micro-batch size b=B/c to CostModeling, but the stated all-forward/all-backward GPipe schedule, with activation checkpointing disabled, retains activations for c micro-batches and therefore scales approximately with c·b=B. The single-max latency expression also merges forward and backward bottlenecks using only a heuristic correlation; it is not the general GPipe makespan.

The repeated claim of finding an optimal strategy is unsupported. The performance model is approximate, Appendix E permits termination at a 4% MIP gap or after 60 seconds, and the complexity analysis hides the NP-hard optimization by treating this timeout as constant. At most, the method returns a bounded-time incumbent for predicted cost, not a proven optimum in actual throughput.

Cost-model validation reports only average error on roughly eight selected final configurations. It does not measure candidate-wide ranking accuracy, top-choice regret, or OOM prediction, which are the quantities needed to validate strategy selection. The meaning of the reported ± values and number of independent trials are also unspecified, and profiling overhead is excluded from optimization time.

Baseline evidence is uneven: Alpa is unavailable or fails on several cases, the 3.80× headline gain comes from one Llama setting, and many ENVA results are ties. The ENVD comparison is against manual Megatron search and a ZeRO-3 configuration that produces no solution, rather than a competitive automatic joint planner.

No code artifact is identified, and essential implementation details—including construction of the strategy dictionary, device-subset mapping, exact resharding/overlap calculations, and the missing polynomial reformulation—are absent. Reliance on commercial Gurobi further limits reproducibility. Moreover, the contribution is principally a distributed-training systems method; two vision throughput benchmarks provide only limited CV-specific impact. These material concerns outweigh the otherwise substantial empirical effort.

strengths: The paper addresses an important practical problem and proposes a unified search over pipeline, data, tensor, and fully sharded data parallelism while accounting for computation, communication, topology, and memory.

The evaluation includes six model configurations from five Transformer families, four hardware environments, and 8–64 accelerators, including both NVIDIA GPUs and DCUs. Several measured gains are meaningful, such as 1.18× on ViT-Huge, 1.37× on Swin-Huge, and 3.80× on Llama-7B in the reported settings.
The manuscript reports actual training throughput and supplements the main comparison with cost-estimation results, scalability experiments, an ablation, and a detailed strategy case study.
The presentation is generally organized and readable, with useful notation, pseudocode, diagrams, and implementation details in the appendix.
weaknesses: The central formulation is not an MIQP as written. Equations (3) and (4) contain terms of the form P_ui P_vi (S_u^T R S_v), which are fourth-degree products of binary variables; the max in Equation (2) is also not reformulated. No auxiliary variables or linearization are provided, so the manuscript does not specify the optimization problem purportedly solved by Gurobi.

The placement constraints do not enforce topological ordering of pipeline stages. For a chain u→v→w, assigning u, v, and w to stages 1, 3, and 2 respectively satisfies the stated per-stage contiguity constraints, while neither edge is charged by Equation (4), which only handles consecutive forward-indexed stages. Thus the stated program admits invalid, under-costed solutions.

The global-optimality claim is unsupported. Equation (2) approximates the GPipe makespan by combining forward and backward bottlenecks based only on a claimed high-probability correlation, while Appendix E permits termination at a 4% MIP gap or after 60 seconds. The complexity analysis likewise hides the NP-hard solver behind a constant time limit; a time-limited solution cannot simultaneously be guaranteed optimal.

The GPipe memory constraint appears incomplete: Algorithm 1 constructs costs using micro-batch size b=B/c, but Equation (5) contains no term for the c forward activations simultaneously retained by a flush-style GPipe schedule, despite activation checkpointing being disabled. This can underestimate peak memory and may relate to the reported CUDA-OOM strategy in Figure 6.

The experiments do not isolate the claimed benefit of joint rather than hierarchical optimization. Figure 6 only compares the full search space against inter-layer-only and intra-layer-only spaces; it lacks a hierarchical search using the same candidates, cost model, and execution backend. A larger feasible set alone predictably produces a no-worse modeled optimum.

The headline evidence is fragile: the 3.80× gain comes from one Llama-7B setting against Galvatron, with Alpa unavailable; on the DCU cluster UniAP only matches Megatron throughput, while DeepSpeed is excluded by the selected batch/device configuration. Framework differences, numerous OOM/N/A entries, and absence of same-backend comparisons further weaken attribution to the proposed optimizer.

Reported optimization time covers only UOP and excludes the required hardware/model profiling and plan construction. The claimed greater-than-107× result also relies on Alpa exceeding a 40-minute cutoff, so it is not an end-to-end planning-time comparison.

Cost-model validation covers only eight selected optimal strategies rather than prediction accuracy or ranking over the candidate space. The scalability tests increase batch size with device count and therefore demonstrate weak scaling, without baseline scaling efficiency.

Reproducibility is limited by the absence of released code and missing details for the actual polynomial reformulation, candidate-strategy dictionary, graph conversion, profiler, CCOC estimation, and number of independent trials. Figure 6's displayed batch sizes also disagree with those stated in Section 4.4.

The contribution is principally distributed-training systems research. ViT and Swin are used as workloads, but no vision-specific method, task result, or insight is contributed, making its relevance to computer vision and pattern recognition indirect for CVPR.

strengths: The paper addresses an important systems problem by jointly selecting pipeline placement and per-layer DP, TP, and FSDP strategies, offering a potentially useful alternative to hierarchical planners.

The evaluation covers diverse hardware—V100, TITAN Xp, A100, and non-NVIDIA DCUs—and six Transformer configurations, including ViT-Huge and Swin-Huge. Reported gains include 1.20–1.71× throughput on several multi-node workloads and 3.80× for Llama-7B on A100s.

The manuscript includes profiling-based computation, communication, resharding, and memory models, along with an ablation, scalability experiments, an interpretable strategy case study, and an average reported estimation error of 3.59%.
The organization, diagrams, tables, notation appendix, and discussion of the selected BERT strategy make the high-level approach relatively accessible.
weaknesses: The central formulation is not an MIQP as written. Equations (3) and (4) contain degree-four products such as P_ui P_vi S_uk S_vl, while the max term in Equation (2) is also left unreformulated. No auxiliary variables or exact linearization constraints are supplied, so the stated formulation cannot directly be given to the cited Gurobi 10.1 MIQP solver.

The purported order-preserving constraints enforce only that every stage's node set is contiguous; they do not order stage indices topologically. For a two-node edge u→v, assigning u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 satisfies the presented contiguity constraints, while Equation (4) misses its communication entirely because it only counts stage j→j+1 edges. Thus the optimization can admit invalid placements with underestimated objectives.

Claims of finding an optimal solution are unsupported. The search restricts pipeline degrees to factors of the GPU count, uses equal-sized device groups, and restricts micro-batch counts; moreover, Gurobi is stopped after 60 seconds or once a gap below 4% is reached. Combined with an approximate cost model, this yields at most a model-predicted incumbent in a restricted space, not the claimed global optimum. The complexity analysis similarly hides the NP-hard solver behind a constant time limit.

The GPipe memory accounting appears inconsistent with the algorithm: CostModeling receives micro-batch size b=B/c, but the memory expression contains no factor for the c simultaneously retained activation sets in fill-drain GPipe, despite activation checkpointing being disabled. This can substantially underestimate peak memory.

The experiments do not establish optimization correctness: there is no exhaustive small-instance comparison, solver-gap reporting, or strategy-ranking analysis. The estimation study evaluates only selected final strategies, and Figure 8 plots signed negative values despite Equation (13) defining a nonnegative absolute error.

Baseline evidence is uneven. Alpa is unavailable, fails, or exceeds the cutoff in most settings; the 3.80× headline gain comes from one Llama/Galvatron comparison; and the DCU results tie Megatron in throughput. Search-time comparisons also favor a multithreaded commercial solver over reportedly single-threaded baselines without controlling solver resources. The scalability experiments increase batch size with device count, demonstrating weak rather than fixed-workload scaling.

Reproducibility is limited by the absence of released code and insufficient specification of the candidate-strategy dictionary, profiling protocol, software stack, solver thread count, and number of repeated trials. The contribution is also primarily distributed-systems research: only two vision architectures are tested, with no vision-specific method or end-to-end accuracy evidence.

strengths: Jointly selecting pipeline placement and per-layer DP/TP/FSDP strategies is a useful systems problem, and the proposed unified search space is more expressive than inter-layer-only or intra-layer-only planning.

The evaluation covers several hardware settings—including multi-node GPUs and up to 64 DCUs—and six Transformer configurations spanning vision and language. UniAP obtains meaningful gains in some settings, most notably 3.80× throughput over Galvatron for Llama-7B.

The paper includes useful supporting analyses: restricted-search ablations, weak-scaling experiments, cost-estimation errors, solver settings, and a topology-aware case study that makes the resulting strategy interpretable.
The manuscript is generally well organized, and its diagrams, notation table, and appendices make the intended optimization workflow understandable.
weaknesses: Material: The central formulation is not an MIQP as written. Equations (3) and (4) contain products of the form P_ui P_vi S_uk S_vl, which are fourth-degree terms. No auxiliary variables or exact linearization are supplied, and the max operator in Equation (2) is also not reformulated. Thus, the stated formulation cannot directly justify the reported use of an MIQP solver.

Material: The constraints do not enforce topological ordering of pipeline stages. For a simple edge u→v, assigning u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 satisfies the placement and per-stage contiguity constraints, while Equation (4) charges communication only from stage j to j+1. Such a reversed assignment can therefore omit communication and represent an invalid execution plan. Edges crossing more than one stage are likewise not modeled.

Material: The repeated claim of finding an optimal strategy is unsupported. Appendix E imposes a 60-second limit and may terminate after 15 seconds with a relative gap below 4%. Moreover, Equation (2) is explicitly approximate, assumes aligned forward/backward bottlenecks, and omits optimizer time. The method can at most claim a bounded or heuristic solution under an estimated cost model.

Material: The complexity analysis hides the NP-hard optimization by declaring the solver timeout constant and consequently reports O(|V||S|√(Bn)). This describes a capped runtime, not the complexity of obtaining the claimed optimum, and it also omits edge-dependent strategy-pair costs.

Material: GPipe memory feasibility is insufficiently specified. Algorithm 1 passes micro-batch size b=B/c to the cost model, while Equation (5) has no explicit factor for the c forward activations retained by a flush-style GPipe schedule without checkpointing. The undefined context-memory term m_c does not establish that these activations or FSDP transient buffers are covered.

The experiments do not validate actual global plan quality. Cost-model error is reported only for the already-selected plans, rather than over candidate plans with ranking correlation or exhaustive ground truth on small instances. There is also no loss/accuracy-parity check confirming that generated hybrid strategies preserve training semantics.

Baseline evidence is uneven. The headline 3.80× gain is one Llama-7B comparison against Galvatron, with Alpa unavailable; the >107× optimization result uses a censored >40-minute baseline. On ENVA, UniAP ties Galvatron on three models, and on the DCU experiments it ties Megatron throughput while DeepSpeed produces no solution. This supports usefulness but not the broad superiority claimed.

Reproducibility is limited by the absence of a code artifact and insufficient specification of the strategy dictionary, profiling protocol, resharding matrices, context memory, device-group construction, and number of independent trials. Reported optimization time measures UOP after profiling, so it does not establish end-to-end planning overhead; reliance on proprietary Gurobi is an additional practical limitation.

The contribution is primarily distributed-training infrastructure rather than computer vision or pattern recognition. Only ViT and Swin experiments connect it to vision, and no vision accuracy, task-level consequence, or vision-specific insight is provided, making the CVPR contribution limited.

Presentation-only issues include inconsistent claims of five versus six evaluated model configurations, a row/column inconsistency when describing S in Appendix D, and several typographical errors. These are readily repairable and are not score-determining.

strengths: The complete manuscript :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-03/reviews/cvpr2025--gpt56_sol/review-experiment-4_yr8qzi/call-1c9dd6fc9b8444adad26a4e46712a232/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"} addresses an important practical problem. Jointly selecting pipeline placement and per-layer DP/TP/FSDP strategies is useful, and the unified optimization perspective is potentially original relative to the hierarchical methods discussed.

The experimental breadth is appreciable: four hardware environments, NVIDIA and non-NVIDIA accelerators, up to 64 devices, and six Transformer configurations spanning vision and language. UniAP provides meaningful gains on several settings, including 1.18–1.71x on three ENVB cases and 3.80x over Galvatron for Llama-7B on ENVC.

The authors measure actual training throughput rather than reporting only modeled costs. The reported 3.59% average throughput-estimation error, compared with 11.17% for Galvatron, offers some support for the cost model.
The restricted-search ablation, scalability experiments, Megatron candidate statistics, and detailed BERT case study provide several complementary views of practical utility.
The paper is generally clear and well organized. Its diagrams, notation table, pseudocode, hardware descriptions, and strategy visualization make the high-level approach accessible.
weaknesses: The central mathematical program is not an MIQP as written. In Eq. (3), P_ui P_vi(S_u^T R_uv S_v), and the analogous term in Eq. (4), contain products of four decision variables; even the first term is bilinear. The max in Eq. (2) also requires an epigraph or general-constraint construction. No auxiliary-variable linearization is provided, so the stated formulation cannot directly be implemented in Gurobi 10.1 as claimed. This is a material specification and reproducibility gap in the core contribution.

The constraints do not enforce the ordering of pipeline-stage indices or account for arbitrary cross-stage edges. For a two-node chain u→v, assigning u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 satisfies the placement and contiguity constraints, yet Eq. (4) charges no communication because it includes only stage j→j+1. Likewise, an edge that skips a stage is ignored. Thus the presented feasible set can admit incorrectly costed pipeline assignments.

The GPipe cost and memory models appear technically inconsistent with the stated schedule. A flushed GPipe makespan generally has separate forward and backward bottleneck maxima, whereas Eq. (2) replaces them with max_i(f_i+b_i), which is exact only when the same stage or link bottlenecks both phases. More seriously, Algorithm 1 passes micro-batch size b=B/c to the memory model, while GPipe without activation checkpointing retains activations for all c forward micro-batches; Eq. (5) contains no corresponding factor c. The paper explicitly says checkpointing is disabled.

Repeated claims of finding an optimal strategy are not supported. Appendix E imposes a 60-second limit and terminates after 15 seconds at a relative MIP gap below 4%, so solutions need not be globally optimal. The search also assumes equal device allocation across stages and enumerates only factor-based pipeline and micro-batch choices. The complexity analysis hides the combinatorial solver behind a constant timeout, conflating bounded runtime with exact polynomial-time optimization.

The evaluation does not independently validate solution optimality. Cost accuracy is shown for only eight selected strategies rather than the wider candidate space whose ranking determines the choice; solver termination gaps/statuses and search regret are not reported; and no small instance is exhaustively enumerated against the proposed optimizer. The ablation compares joint search only with inter-layer-only and intra-layer-only spaces, not with a controlled hierarchical joint-search baseline.

The headline gains are less general than the abstract suggests: the 3.80x result is one Llama configuration; UniAP ties Galvatron on three ENVA models and is slightly slower for T5 on ENVB; Alpa is unavailable or fails on several cases; and the DCU results match Megatron throughput while improving search time. Optimization-time comparisons also give multithreaded commercial Gurobi an early-stopping rule while baselines are described as single-threaded, without equal CPU budgets or inclusion of profiling overhead.

Reproduction would be difficult because no implementation link is supplied, the actual higher-order reformulation and strategy-dictionary construction are absent, and software versions, profiling workload, CPU/thread budgets, solver gaps per run, and the number and meaning of reported repetitions are incompletely specified. The contribution is also primarily a distributed-training systems result; its direct computer-vision evidence is limited to throughput on ViT-Huge and Swin-Huge. These concerns outweigh the promising empirical results in the manuscript's current form.

strengths: The joint optimization of pipeline placement and per-layer DP, TP, and FSDP choices addresses an important, practically useful problem and is more unified than the hierarchical baselines considered.

The evaluation uses real execution across four heterogeneous hardware environments and up to 64 accelerators, rather than relying solely on simulation. On ENVB-8, UniAP improves ViT-Huge throughput from 38.74 to 45.58 samples/s and Swin-Huge from 13.90 to 19.08 samples/s relative to the strongest available baseline.

The paper supports its main intuition with a restricted-search-space ablation, scalability experiments, a topology-aware case study, and cost-model validation reporting 3.59% average estimation error.
The large Llama-7B gain on eight A100 GPUs—4.63 versus 1.22 samples/s—demonstrates that jointly selecting pipeline and intra-layer strategies can matter substantially in some configurations.

The manuscript is generally well organized, and the appendix usefully documents notation, the contiguity proof, model configurations, solver settings, and the discovered BERT strategy. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-03/reviews/cvpr2025--gpt56_sol/review-experiment-__wv5u9k/call-4f8947774788468489cb08e5a601d33b/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}
weaknesses: Material: the optimization is not an MIQP as written. Terms such as P_ui P_vi(S_u^T R_uv S_v) contain products of four binary variables, and the max term in the objective is not reformulated. Auxiliary variables and their linking constraints would be needed, but neither the formulation nor implementation explains them.

Material: contiguity of each stage does not enforce precedence between numbered stages. A directed edge can be assigned backward or across nonconsecutive stages, in which case it contributes to neither the within-stage term nor Equation (4). Thus, the stated program can omit required communication and admit invalid pipeline assignments.

Material: the repeated claim of finding an optimal strategy is unsupported. Gurobi may stop after 60 seconds or at a 4% MIP gap, the cost model is approximate, and the search restricts pipeline sizes, microbatch counts, and candidate strategies. The complexity analysis also treats the capped MIQP solve as constant time while claiming optimality.

Material: Algorithm 1 passes microbatch size b=B/c to the memory model, while Equation (5) contains no factor for the multiple activations simultaneously retained by the illustrated GPipe schedule. Unless an undocumented implementation correction exists, activation memory can be underestimated by roughly the number of in-flight microbatches.

Evidence: cost-model accuracy is tested only on the selected strategies, not across candidates whose ranking determines planner quality; no small exhaustive experiment verifies optimal selection. Figure 8 also displays negative values although Equation (13) defines an absolute, nonnegative error.

Reproducibility and scope: no UniAP code is provided, and important details of strategy enumeration, graph construction, resharding costs, software versions, profiling overhead, and trial counts are missing. The headline optimization-time comparison measures UOP after profiling and is partly driven by baseline OOM/N/A cases. Moreover, the contribution is primarily a general distributed-systems method, with direct CV evidence limited to ViT and Swin. These concerns leave the paper near the acceptance boundary despite promising empirical utility.
